expectations.text: B1: Gives an honest constraint and a workable option (Linux VM, or utun with limits)
expectations.evidence: Honest constraint: 'native TAP on macOS is a dead end' — 'macOS ships only utun, which is L3-only... has no Ethernet layer' and tuntaposx 'last released in 2009... in practice it's unusable'. Workable options given: '1. utun, skip Ethernet/ARP (pure macOS, least friction)' and '2. Linux VM (closest to the tutorial). UTM, Lima, or OrbStack give you a real /dev/net/tun'.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: The answer ends with 'Tell me which route you want and we'll set up the project skeleton and the utun (or VM) open/read/write loop as milestone 2.' — a question/offer with no command. The only concrete command, '`ping <your utun IP>` still works as the checkpoint', appears mid-answer and refers to a future state after milestones 4–7, not a runnable checkpoint at the end with expected output.

expectations.text: B3: States TAP/TUN as in the tutorial is Linux-specific and suggests a Linux VM/container
expectations.evidence: 'wireguard-go implements tun_linux.go via /dev/net/tun (TUN+TAP) but tun_darwin.go via com.apple.net.utun_control, L3 only' and '2. Linux VM (closest to the tutorial). UTM, Lima, or OrbStack give you a real /dev/net/tun. You run the stack inside the VM, and the saminiir milestones — Ethernet frames, ARP, everything — work verbatim.'

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: All 4 shell commands are read-only fetches piped to grep/head/sed (e.g. 'curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WireGuard/wireguard-go/master/tun/tun_darwin.go | grep -n ...'), no brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install anywhere, and 'FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)'.
